name: Medora Hotel (Coleman & Brown boarding house and restaurant)
evidence: Lot bought June 19, 1884; nearly done July 3; ad Nov 20, 1884 (Cow Boy).

name: Company barn, stable and corral (Deffebach livery)
evidence: Rented to Bassie Deffebach as a livery (May 1884); additional barn south of the old one (March 1885) (Cow Boy).

name: Gill Kennedy's oyster restaurant
evidence: Building moved from the west side to John Warn's old lot, Sept 1885; ice-house south of it (Cow Boy).

name: John O'Sullivan's barber shop and house
evidence: "next to John Warn's" (Cow Boy 1884-06-19); Lot 11, Block 19 (Cow Boy 1885-09, to re-check: the Sept 1885 item is the Kennedy restaurant moving to "where John Warn's restaurant stood"). Block 19 is not in today's parcel layer.

name: McKenzie & O'Brien blacksmith shop
evidence: Moved to the north side of the track, May 1885; sold to Alex Morton 1886 (Cow Boy).

name: W. B. Pryor's shoe shop
evidence: On a lot "near the church," March-April 1885 (Cow Boy).

name: C. F. Ellison's house by the Catholic church
NP coal mine and powder house
evidence: Coal mine roof caving in (Cow Boy 1884-06-12); old powder-house north of the track. Historic Medora "Coal Mining" panel: the Northern Pacific Coal Co. mine "just west of Medora" closed in 1884 and "a new mine opened at the base of the butte on the east side of Medora". The west-side mine is the plat's coal mine (placed); the 1884 east-side mine is not yet located.

name: Merchants National Bank (planned)
evidence: Four lots at the corner of Third Street and Broadway bought April 1884; again planned "on the vacant hotel square" in 1885; never reported built (Cow Boy).

name: Stockyards
evidence: Old NP yards "across the river" were too small; a small yard 50x50, then 100x100 (Cow Boy 1885-04-16); new yards where the cattle "round the butte at the brick-kiln", with the river, butte and railroad as pen walls (Cow Boy 1885-10-22).

name: Paddock's building for the Boston clothing house
evidence: Nearly finished June 1885 (Cow Boy 1885-06-25); Paddock's residence moved to Dickinson in sections June 1887.

name: Sylvane Ferris's house
evidence: SHSND 00129-10002 (Reichensperger collection; catalogue date 1885; back reads "Col. 00129-00012 Built by Sylvane Ferris"): a front-gabled two-story block with a bay window and a one-story wing with full front porch, picket fence, directly under a tall banded butte, so it stood at the foot of the east or south bluffs. Its 1885 date is the catalogue's; the photo itself may be later (two-story frame house, young planted trees). A Dickinson Museum Center caption begins "His house became the ..." and is cut off. Whether it survives is unknown - a local check would settle it.

name: De Mores rental houses ("Houses to be let")
evidence: shsnd:00042-00030 etc.; St. Paul Daily Globe 1884-02-13 mentions "numerous small residence houses."

name: De Mores brick business block (planned)
evidence: Two store rooms below, offices above (St. Paul Daily Globe 1884-02-13). Was it built?

name: Gifford Bros. & Co. general store, Little Missouri
Other 1883 Little Missouri saloons (Smith & Stevens; Edgar & Saebastian; J. J. Smith)
Paddock's cabin and livery, Little Missouri
evidence: "'Little Misery.' Paddock's cabin in foreground, 1880" (Haynes, in NPSHB).
